stories.title: Start the whole stack with one Docker Compose command

story.want: to start Banyan with `docker compose up -d --build`
story.so: every environment is reproducible and the MVP can be released from one artefact

stories.businessContext: The repository has a single Dockerfile and no Compose file. The brief's release criteria require the full application to start under Docker Compose.
functionalRequirements: Compose services: web (Next.js UI + API), worker, postgres, redis
Named volume for Postgres data that survives `docker compose down`
Internal network; only web publishes a host port
Health checks on every service; web depends on healthy postgres and redis
Restart policy `unless-stopped`
nonFunctionalRequirements: Security: no secrets in the Compose file; all from .env
Reliability: services restart on failure; graceful shutdown on SIGTERM
Performance: cold start under 90 s on a developer laptop
acceptanceCriteria: Given a clean checkout and a filled .env, When I run `docker compose up -d --build`, Then `docker compose ps` shows web, worker, postgres and redis as healthy
Given the stack is running, When I run `docker compose down` and `up -d` again, Then my workspace data is still there
Given postgres is not yet healthy, When web starts, Then web waits instead of crashing

technicalImplementation.jobs: worker service runs the queue consumer (US-006)

testScenarios.happy: compose up, all services healthy, GET /api/health returns ok
testScenarios.validation: missing APP_SECRET in .env makes web exit with a clear message
testScenarios.authorization: postgres and redis ports not reachable from the host
testScenarios.external: stop postgres: web health turns unhealthy, recovers when postgres returns

stories.evidence: 2026-11-01: `docker compose up -d --build` → postgres/redis healthy, migrate Exited (0), web healthy, worker up; postgres and redis publish no host port; missing POSTGRES_PASSWORD/APP_SECRET refused at `compose config`; users 2 → 2 across down/up; web unhealthy when postgres stopped and healthy again on restart; worker restarted by Compose after SIGTERM; E2E 42/42 against the stack

stories.title: Durable job queue on Redis

story.want: to enqueue background work durably
story.so: slow or external operations never block a request and survive restarts

stories.businessContext: Background work today is triggered by an HTTP tick every 60 s (TD-02). The brief requires Redis-backed background jobs (ADR-002).
functionalRequirements: Queue module: enqueue(job, payload, {delay, attempts, backoff}), consume(handler)
Jobs survive a worker restart
Failed jobs move to a dead-letter set after max attempts
Job ids are deterministic where the operation is idempotent
nonFunctionalRequirements: Reliability: at-least-once delivery; handlers must be idempotent (enforced by Postgres unique keys)
Security: Redis not exposed outside the Compose network
acceptanceCriteria: Given a job is enqueued, When the worker restarts before processing it, Then it is processed after the restart
Given a job fails three times, When the max attempts is reached, Then it is in the dead-letter set with its last error
Given the same idempotent job is enqueued twice, When processed, Then the side effect happens once

technicalImplementation.jobs: Defines the queue all other jobs use

testScenarios.external: Redis down: enqueue fails loudly, request returns 503
testScenarios.retry: handler throws twice then succeeds; processed once

stories.evidence: 2026-11-01: BullMQ queue (src/lib/queue); 19 unit tests (payload validation, deterministic job ids, dead-letter retention, fails loudly without Redis); live: delayed job held in Redis and processed after a worker restart

functionalRequirements: Worker consumes publication, status-sync and analysis jobs

The existing tick endpoint remains as a safety sweep for anything missed
Graceful shutdown finishes the in-flight job
nonFunctionalRequirements: Reliability: duplicate execution guarded by Publication.idempotencyKey
Performance: due job starts within 5 s
acceptanceCriteria: Given an approved post scheduled for 10:00, When it is 10:00, Then the publication attempt starts within 5 s
Given the worker is stopped at 10:00, When it starts at 10:03, Then the post is attempted once

technicalImplementation.backend: worker/index.ts becomes a queue consumer; schedule route enqueues
technicalImplementation.integration: Distribution provider called from the job

testScenarios.retry: worker killed mid-job → job re-delivered, published once
